$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the only one that reaches scoreVerdict's unmeasurable branch,
and without it that branch is unreachable from the corpus and nothing would notice it being deleted.
The branch used to fire whenever a report declared more violations than it attributed to registry
rows, which is a shape the CLI parser explicitly permits for Medium and Low, so four cases sat on it
for the wrong reason. Now it fires on one condition only: the verdict carries no findings array, so
there is no reported list to compare with the plants.
The verdict is CONSTRUCTED. The report it names is the same real capture unattributed-violations
reads, and this verdict differs from that one by exactly the absent key.
derivation: scoreVerdict tests Array.isArray(verdict.findings) before it reads anything else. The key is absent,
so the test is false and it returns null. Nothing about the ground truth enters the arithmetic: no
plant is consulted, no line is compared, and the run is unscoreable before matching begins.
An empty findings array is a different answer and unattributed-violations records it: [] is a
reviewer that named nothing, which is a measured miss on a corpus with nine planted defects. Absent
is a verdict this CLI did not write. The distinction is the whole case.
